questions: Did s-bend progress rise clearly above 0.1604 at wheel_track 0.09 m, and did its max_error stay at or below 0.063 m?
Did steering_oscillation stay below 0.16 on all tracks? In particular, is slalom oscillation below 0.16 (it was 0.157 at 0.10 m)? If not, reduce kp before any further geometry change.
Did the oval hold progress near 0.167 and rms_error near 0.019, with line-loss events near 0.95?
Did any track complete? If not, which track ends off track first, and at what progress?
Did line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom stay at one per run, or fall?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this layout, and which sensors carry most signal when on the line.

intent: Continue the drivetrain test from iteration 8 with a smaller step: wheel_track 0.09 m (from 0.10 m), keeping the seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.08 m, mass 0.8 kg, radius 0.03 m and body 0.12 × 0.16 m. The aim is to lift s-bend progress clearly above 0.16 while keeping steering_oscillation below 0.16 on every track, especially the slalom, which is at 0.157.
learning: Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.10 m) gave the first clean drivetrain gain: s-bend progress 0.1496 to 0.1604, oval 0.161 to 0.167, score 57.50 to 60.32, with all oscillation below 0.16. The slalom oscillation of 0.157 is now the binding constraint on further turn-rate increases. The next step tests 0.09 m, a smaller change than the contract minimum, so the result can separate a real progress trend from the oscillation limit. If the result is flat, the drivetrain lever is exhausted at 0.10 m.
rationale:
Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.10 m, everything else as iteration 7) scored 60.32, up from 57.50. The change helped on every track. The s-bend rose from 0.1496 to 0.1604 progress with max_error 0.0613 m. The oval rose from 0.161 to 0.167 with rms_error 0.0193. Slalom progress rose from 0.1064 to 0.110. Line-loss events were 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom and 0.95 on the oval, so no new loss appeared. All steering_oscillation values stayed below 0.16: oval 0.109, s-bend 0.145, slalom 0.157. Slalom oscillation is now close to the trigger.

The s-bend gain is small, about 7 percent, and it does not yet clearly clear 0.16. The Integrator's rule allows a test at 0.08 m, the contract minimum. I do not think that is the right step. Turn rate scales roughly with 1/wheel_track, so 0.10 to 0.08 m adds about 25 percent more turn rate. Going from 0.12 to 0.10 m (about 20 percent) raised slalom oscillation by about 0.012. A further 25 percent step would likely push slalom oscillation to about 0.17, past the trigger, and cost the controller stability it needs.

I therefore choose wheel_track 0.09 m as a cautious step. It probes whether s-bend progress keeps rising with turn rate, with a smaller expected increase in oscillation. Mass stays at 0.8 kg, since the 0.6 kg mass in iteration 4 was confounded and the gain from mass is not isolated. Sensing stays at seven contiguous 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.048 m and y = 0.08 m, because pitch and forward lead have been tested and are not the limit.

Expected result: s-bend progress about 0.16 to 0.165, oval about 0.165 with line loss near 0.95, and slalom oscillation about 0.15 to 0.165. If slalom oscillation exceeds 0.16 with line loss unchanged, the Integrator should reduce kp before further geometry change. If the s-bend is flat or worse, revert to wheel_track 0.10 m, which is the best measured geometry so far (score 60.32).
